data.title: Everolimus for the treatment of neuropsychological deficits in tuberous sclerosis complex: findings from the TRON multicentre randomised controlled trial
data.authors: Saxena A; Drew CJ; Cannings-John R; Pickles T; Mills LJ; Sampson JR et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: In a multicentre RCT of TSC patients (n=38 randomised, 2:1 everolimus:placebo), 24 weeks of everolimus produced similarly large 'responder' rates for neuropsychological improvement as placebo (87% vs 75%), suggesting large practice/placebo effects rather than a clear drug benefit on cognition -- despite everolimus's established efficacy for TSC tumours and epilepsy. Adverse events were more frequent with everolimus (88% vs 61.5%).
data.abstract_excerpt: Mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitors are effective treatments for tumours and epilepsy in tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC). This study aimed to determine the effects of the mTOR inhibitor everolimus and a placebo on neuropsychological functioning in TSC. Individuals with TSC aged 16-60 years and IQ>60 who scored <=5th percentile in one or more of 10 memory or executive function variables were randomised 2:1 to 24 weeks everolimus or placebo and retested at baseline and 4, 12, 24 and 36 weeks.

extracted_findings.intervention: Everolimus (mTOR inhibitor) vs placebo, 24 weeks, randomised 2:1
extracted_findings.effect: No clear benefit of everolimus over placebo on neuropsychological function; both arms showed large responder rates (87% vs 75%), likely reflecting practice/placebo effects rather than a true drug effect
